text:
FANTASY GAME THEORY:

🎓🎓🎓

Let’s talk about building a “league-winning” roster.

Most of the discussion around this topic centers around chasing “UPSIDE.”

While I agree with this core principle – the principle is often used to hijack the entire conversation – to the point where players who “only beat their ADP by a few spots” are actually viewed as “bad” picks.

Essentially – if a player isn’t a “league-winning” pick, they’re a “bad” pick.

This notion is used to dismiss “boring” but productive veterans – all the time.

I’d like to challenge this notion of them being “bad” picks – as it simply is not supported by the data.

Via @RyanJ_Heath’s “Anatomy of a League-Winner” series…

We know that:

There were 18 “league-winning” players in 2024.

There were 18 “league-winning” players in 2025.

Essentially – we get 18 “league-winning” players per season.

(“League-winner” being defined as a player to make 55%+ of playoff rosters, using leagues where 4 out of 10 leagues make playoffs as the baseline)

Out of the 18 "league-winners" in 2025 – 13/18 (72.2%) were drafted within the first 5 rounds.

Out of the 18 “league-winners” in 2024 – 17/18 (94.4%) were drafted inside the first 6 rounds; all of the QB's/RB's/WR's (15/15) inside the first 5 rounds.

In total – 30/36 “league-winners” (83.3%) over the last 2 seasons have been drafted inside the first 6 rounds.

Essentially – you only need “league-winners” with your first 5-6 picks.

& your goal with your remaining 8-10 picks should quite literally be:

“To draft players who slightly outperform their ADP’s – while avoiding players who slightly underperform them.”

This does not apply to the QB position – where you still have a 10%+ chance historically at drafting a league-winner in RD9-12; this is the one position you should still be targeting “league-winners” outside of RD1-5.

Otherwise – you simply want to beat ADP in RD6-12.

Once you get to your last 2-3 picks – you can shift back towards prioritizing only “UPSIDE” – as floor is nonexistent that late.

Your mindset should shift & evolve throughout the draft.

Instead of simply “swinging for a league-winner” at every available pick, I believe the optimal strategy is to:

📌 Target “league-winners” RD1-5
📌 Beat ADP RD6-12 (outside of QB)
📌 Target “league-winners” RD13+

Not exclusively – but as a general guideline.

Your scope should widen from targeting league-winners early, to also including ADP-beaters in the middle rounds, back towards prioritizing upside-only with your last few picks.

Your strategy should shift based on the portion of the draft you’re in.

THAT’s how you craft a true “league-winning” roster.

I understand not wanting to take zeros…

But do you remember last year when people refused to draft Quinshon Judkins in the double-digit rounds?

Because of the “suspension risk.”

Only for those who took that “risk” to end up with a high-volume starter in RD10+

Well – that might just be Josh Jacobs this year (if he’s suspended for only 6 games or less & comes back this season).

I promise you – floor does not matter in the double-digit rounds.

These are the players who were being drafted outside the Top-125 picks last year… how many of them hit??

You should be shooting for UPSIDE only.
